assessment.nobel_worthiness: A new class of quantum matter with protected edge and surface states: theory of the quantum spin Hall effect, then clean experimental realization in HgTe quantum wells. Original, conceptually clear, and it reshaped condensed matter physics and materials discovery. It is a discovery in the sense of the prize criteria, not a lifetime body of work.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele proposed the Z2 topological insulator and the spin Hall state in graphene; Molenkamp's group delivered the decisive quantum spin Hall measurement in HgTe. Hasan's three-dimensional topological insulator observations are also central and the three-person cap forces a hard choice. Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang's HgTe prediction is not in the credited names, so the theory-experiment chain is incomplete.
assessment.maturity: Independently confirmed by many groups across two-dimensional and three-dimensional materials, spectroscopy, transport and later quantum anomalous Hall realizations. The interpretation is stable and recognition is timely, even late.
uncertainties: Whether Mele or Hasan should displace one of the three allocated names is unresolved.
Credit for the HgTe prediction lies partly outside the supplied names.
I rely on my own recollection of the history and have not verified it independently.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Atomic force microscopy with qPlus sensors and CO-functionalized tips resolves the internal bond structure of single molecules. This is a genuine invention that opened a new route to imaging and characterizing matter at the atomic scale, and from my microscopy background I see it as a clear and lasting instrument advance with direct reach into surface physics, chemistry and nanoscience.
assessment.attribution: Giessibl invented the qPlus sensor; Meyer, Gross and colleagues demonstrated the functionalized-tip imaging of molecular structure. The three names map reasonably onto sensor invention and its decisive application, though the underlying scanning-probe lineage (Binnig, Quate, Gerber) was already recognized and Hirjibe-style contributors to tip functionalization are not listed.
assessment.maturity: Widely adopted and reproduced in many laboratories over more than a decade. The method is mature and its interpretation is stable. A measurement-technique prize is plausible and timely given the precedent of recognizing microscopy innovations.
uncertainties: Whether the committee judges this a physics discovery or invention with sufficient fundamental breadth rather than a refinement of an already awarded scanning-probe technology.
Tip-functionalization credit may extend beyond the three names supplied.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices realize controllable many-body Hamiltonians, with the Mott insulator transition as the landmark demonstration and single-site-resolved quantum gas microscopy as a later step. Original in both concept and experiment, with lasting influence across condensed matter, quantum information and precision methods.
assessment.attribution: Zoller (with Jaksch and Cirac) supplied the theoretical proposal, Greiner and Bloch the decisive Mott insulator experiment and later microscopy, and Esslinger the Fermi-Hubbard work. Jaksch is not credited, and Cirac, Esslinger and others are strong alternatives, so a three-person cap leaves real allocation tension.
assessment.maturity: Well established and independently reproduced by many groups; quantum simulation continues to mature, so the field is still developing but the core discovery is secure.
uncertainties: The three-name cap makes allocation among Bloch, Greiner, Zoller, Cirac and Esslinger contested.
The prize may be better framed as a compound of proposal and experiments with different recipients.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Flat bands at the magic angle and the observed correlated insulating and superconducting states in twisted bilayer graphene opened moire quantum materials, a highly active field. It combines a clear theoretical prediction with a striking experimental discovery.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted the flat band; Jarillo-Herrero's group reported the correlated insulator and superconductivity. Andrei's group made early related observations and its role is a credible competing claim.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced by multiple groups and spawned many follow-on phenomena, but the microscopic pairing mechanism and some interpretations are still debated, so the field is less settled than the oldest candidates.
uncertainties: The origin of superconductivity is unsettled.
Andrei's claim and the role of sample-dependent behavior complicate attribution.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock combines the magic-wavelength idea with trapped neutral atoms for extreme stability and accuracy, opening relativistic geodesy tests and redefinition of the second. A clear, concrete invention with strong metrological consequences.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept; Ye's group demonstrated record-setting clocks with strontium. A two-person configuration is clean, though Wineland's ion clock recognition and other optical clock groups form a shared background.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by multiple national laboratories and approaching a redefinition of the SI second, so impact is established and timing is reasonable.
uncertainties: The relation to previously recognized optical frequency comb and ion-clock prizes may lower novelty in the eyes of some members.
Other clock groups' contributions are not credited here.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit quantum electrodynamics created a platform for strong light-matter coupling and quantum readout with superconducting circuits, and underpins most superconducting quantum processors. A consequential discovery with wide uptake.
assessment.attribution: Blais supplied the theory proposal, Wallraff the first strong-coupling demonstration and Schoelkopf the broad development of the architecture. The credited names support a three-person prize, but the 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum effects in superconducting circuits already covers adjacent ground.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced widely and technologically mature; recognition is timely though possibly constrained by the recent related prize.
uncertainties: Overlap with the most recent superconducting-circuit prize may reduce appetite.
Distinct roles of transmon and cQED architecture contributors may need separate recognition.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Room-temperature tunnel magnetoresistance and giant effects in crystalline MgO junctions are a materials-driven invention with large technological reach in magnetic sensing and memory, following the giant magnetoresistance prize. The role of crystalline interface structure resonates with interface-focused electron microscopy work.
assessment.attribution: Moodera reported room-temperature TMR, Parkin and Yuasa independently demonstrated giant TMR in MgO junctions; Miyazaki also made early observations and is excluded by the three-name cap.
assessment.maturity: Mature and commercially deployed, though a physics prize on a second spintronic effect may be seen as incremental after 2007.
uncertainties: Miyazaki's early priority and the cap on laureates leave attribution contested.
Incremental relation to the prior GMR prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: High-gain X-ray free-electron lasers deliver femtosecond coherent X-rays, enabling structural dynamics studies across materials and biology. Strong enabling instrument with broad scientific outcomes.
assessment.attribution: The self-amplified spontaneous emission concept and its high-gain theory are associated with Pellegrini and Kim; Rossbach's TESLA FEL work is a plausible third but I limit the proposal to two. Contributions from Bonifacio, Saldin and the LCLS teams are not in the supplied names, so credit is incomplete.
assessment.maturity: Operating facilities worldwide confirm the technology; recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Attribution for SASE and facility realization is complex and partly outside the credited names.
It may be viewed as accelerator engineering, not a single discovery.
